2607.28488.title: SCOPE: Supply-Chain Operations through Coupled Policies for End-to-End Coordination
2607.28488.paper_summary: Can supply-chain AI move beyond isolated decision modules toward unified operational planning? A complete replenishment plan specifies which products each location carries, which upstream facility supplies it, how often it is replenished, and how deliveries are routed. These decisions are operationally coupled: the selected assortment changes the demand and load passed to later stages; source assignment and replenishment frequency reshape the delivery requests; and route feasibility and cost, in turn, determine the system value of the earlier choices. Yet in modern supply chains, these decisions are often handled by separate departments and optimized through separate systems, which can lead to stockouts, inventory exposure, and avoidable transportation. We propose SCOPE: Supply-Chain Operations through Coupled Policies for End-to-End Coordination, a composite policy model that represents supply-chain entities as tokens, contextualizes them through a shared operational representation, and maps each token type to the corresponding decision interface. Each decision builds on the partial plan formed by earlier decisions while the completed plan is evaluated using a shared system-level utility. We instantiate this framework in urban fresh-retail replenishment, where service frequency, assortment, capacity pressure, and road-network routing interact strongly, and evaluate it on real operational data from Dingdong and JD.com, two large-scale supply chains operating at different replenishment echelons. Across both settings, SCOPE consistently outperforms methods that optimize each decision stage separately, as well as practice-oriented baselines commonly used in supply-chain operations. These results show that learning and coordinating cross-department operational couplings lead to more effective end-to-end supply-chain decisions.
2607.28488.paper_summary_zh: 供應鏈人工智慧能否超越孤立的決策模塊，朝向統一的運營規劃？完整的補貨計劃指定每個地點攜帶哪些產品、由哪個上游設施供應、補貨的頻率以及配送的路徑。這些決策在運營上是相互關聯的：選擇的產品組合改變了後續階段的需求和負載；來源分配和補貨頻率重塑了配送請求；而路徑的可行性和成本又反過來決定了早期選擇的系統價值。然而在現代供應鏈中，這些決策通常由不同部門處理，並通過不同系統進行優化，這可能導致缺貨、庫存暴露和不必要的運輸。我們提出了SCOPE：通過耦合政策進行端到端協調的供應鏈運營，一種將供應鏈實體表示為標記的綜合政策模型，通過共享的運營表示對其進行上下文化，並將每種類型的標記映射到相應的決策界面。每個決策都基於早期決策形成的部分計劃，而完成的計劃則通過共享的系統級效用進行評估。我們在城市生鮮零售補貨中實現了這一框架，在這裡，服務頻率、產品組合、容量壓力和道路網絡路由之間相互強烈影響，並在來自丁丁和京東的真實運營數據上進行評估，這兩個大型供應鏈在不同的補貨層級上運作。在這兩種環境中，SCOPE始終優於分別優化每個決策階段的方法，以及供應鏈運營中常用的以實踐為導向的基準。這些結果顯示，學習和協調跨部門的運營耦合能夠導致更有效的端到端供應鏈決策。
